topIssues.title: JSON POST to /api/tts/cloud 400s on the bare agent server: attachJsonBodyIfPresent consumes the stream the handler re-reads
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Found while capturing live TTS evidence for #16324. On the bare agent server (`packages/agent/src/bin.ts`), `POST /api/tts/cloud` with `Content-Type: application/json` returns 400 'Invalid JSON request body': `attachJsonBodyIfPresent` (`packages/agent/src/api/runtime-plugin-routes.ts:197`) reads the stream and attaches `req.body`, but `handleCloudTtsPreviewRoute` (`plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/lib/server-cloud-tts.ts:91`) re-streams `req` and gets zero bytes. `readCompatJsonBody` in app-core honors pre-parsed `req.body` — the plugin route should do the same. Workaround that sidesteps the pre-read: `Content-Type: text/plain` with a JSON body. The packaged app path re-streams via `dispatch-route.ts` and is unaffected.

topIssues.title: fix(voice): evidence-harness Cartesia server misses the buffer-delay cap #16607 shipped
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Gaps from #16607 (merged)

### [medium] Evidence-harness reference voice server still opens Cartesia without the buffer-delay cap

packages/tools/voice-evidence-harness/src/reference/voice-session-server.ts:436 on origin/develop calls createStream({ traceId: state.traceId }, ...) with no maxBufferDelayMs, then streams sentence-by-sentence with open contexts at line 497 (tts.sendPhrase({ text, continueContext: !last })) — the exact continue:true streaming pattern the PR root-caused as stacking Cartesia's 3000ms default aggregation window. The alias @harness-adapters/cartesia-sonic-tts.ts resolves (voice-evidence-harness tsconfig.json paths) to the same packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/cartesia-sonic-tts.ts adapter that supports the option (CartesiaSonicStreamOptions.maxBufferDelayMs, line 68), so the cap is available and simply not passed. This file is the LIVE-provider §7-contract reference implementation used to produce latency evidence (its header: drives the REAL adapters against LIVE Cartesia); any multi-sentence reply measured through it still incurs the ~2.7s llm_first_text→speaking_start inflation, di

**Fix direction:** Pass the same cap in the reference server: createStream({ traceId: state.traceId, maxBufferDelayMs: 250 }, ...) — ideally importing/sharing the VOICE_TTS_MAX_BUFFER_DELAY_MS constant (export it from session.ts or a shared voice constants module) so harness evidence stays parity with production; then run the harness live once to capture the post-fix speaking_start timing the PR currently lacks.

### [low] New lifecycle test filters out requests missing max_buffer_delay_ms, under-enforcing the claimed invariant

packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/__tests__/ws-lifecycle.test.ts:473-479 on origin/develop: requests = cartesia.sent.map(JSON.parse).filter((entry) => entry.max_buffer_delay_ms !== undefined) then expects length > 0 and each value === 250. The PR body claims the test 'asserts every generation request carries max_buffer_delay_ms=250', but a generation request that OMITS the field is silently excluded by the filter, so only presence-on-at-least-one is enforced. The at-risk path is real: the cap only reaches continuation/terminal requests through the adapter's per-request fallback (packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/cartesia-sonic-tts.ts:432, phrase.maxBufferDelayMs ?? this.input.maxBufferDelayMs); if that fallback were narrowed to first-request-only (or a per-phrase override of undefined were introduced), continuation requests would drop the field, Cartesia's 3000ms window would return for streamed clauses, and this test would stay green.

**Fix direction:** Select generation requests positively instead of by field presence — e.g. filter on entry.model_id !== undefined (or transcript !== undefined) to exclude only the cancel frame {context_id, cancel:true} — and assert max_buffer_delay_ms === 250 on every one, matching the invariant stated in the PR body.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The reference voice server used by evidence runs opens Cartesia with the same `max_buffer_delay_ms` cap as production
- [ ] The lifecycle test asserts the param on EVERY connect request instead of filtering out requests missing it

topIssues.title: fix(chat): cold-open sendActionMessage still blocks on the redundant conversation round trip
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Gap from #16619 (merged)

### [medium] Sibling cold-open send path sendActionMessage still blocks on the redundant conversation create

packages/ui/src/state/useChatSend.ts:2262-2269 (origin/develop): in sendActionMessage, `if (!convId) { ... await client.createConversation(actionTitle || t("common.newChat")) }` runs before the message dispatch — the exact serialized cold Worker/Hyperdrive round trip the PR removes from runQueuedChatSend (which now calls createConversationForFirstSend at useChatSend.ts:1423). The path's own error comment at useChatSend.ts:2285-2287 says it 'mirrors the cold-open path in runQueuedChatSend'. For a direct shared-agent base the create is provably redundant: the server POST handler (packages/cloud/api/v1/eliza/agents/[agentId]/api/conversations/route.ts:42-56) never reads the request body, so the actionTitle is discarded and the response is the same synthesizable canonical record (shared-rest-adapter.ts:57-68, id === agentId). A weaker sibling exists at packages/ui/src/state/useChatCallbacks.ts:940-948 (bare new-chat create, not the bootstrapGreeting flow at line 322 that the PR body says i

**Fix direction:** Route sendActionMessage's cold-open create through createConversationForFirstSend (extend the helper with an optional title forwarded only to the real chatClient.createConversation fallback — the shared-agent server ignores titles anyway), so action/inbox first sends on shared agents skip the round trip like ordinary first sends.

## Also (low): client-synthesized conversation diverges from the server-canonical record (title/createdAt); Server-Timing absent on 400/auth responses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sendActionMessage` gets the same deferred-create treatment as the fixed send path
- [ ] Cold-open action send round-trip count matches the fixed path's

topIssues.title: fix(auth): durable PWA pair token has no invalidation path
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Gap from #16620 (merged)

### [medium] Durable pair token has no invalidation/clear path anywhere (write got a durable channel, delete never added)

Repo-wide grep: only 4 files reference "eliza:cloud-pair:api-token" (packages/ui/src/components/auth/CloudPairRelay.tsx, packages/app/src/main.tsx, packages/agent/src/api/cloud-pair-route.ts, packages/app-core/src/api/cloud-pair-route.ts) and none call removeItem/clear on it. The stale-token failure path never purges it: packages/ui/src/App.tsx:2759-2780 renders CloudHostedAgentAuthNotice on unauthenticated, and packages/ui/src/hooks/useAgentSessionRecovery.ts:89-102 drops to "idle" without touching storage when recovery cannot proceed. Meanwhile packages/app/src/main.tsx:463 re-adopts the dead localStorage token on every launch, stamps it as the client bearer (main.tsx:487), and re-persists it into the active-server + agent-profile stores (main.tsx:493-505). Pre-PR the token was session-scoped so it self-evicted; post-PR a rotated/revoked ELIZA_API_TOKEN (agent re-provision, secret rotation — the PR body itself only proves the blue/green upgrade path preserves it) leaves a permanently

**Fix direction:** Clear the key from both storages (and stop re-persisting it into the active-server/profile stores) when the auth probe 401s and useAgentSessionRecovery ends idle — i.e., right where CloudHostedAgentAuthNotice is chosen in App.tsx — and/or add an explicit disconnect action on the notice that removes eliza:cloud-pair:api-token before linking back to Cloud.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sign-out / unpair / agent-deletion clears the durable pair token (delete channel symmetric with the write channel)
- [ ] (low) Boot resolver gates adoption on origin/platform before stamping

topIssues.title: fix(orchestrator): ACP readiness fail-open siblings — pi-agent missing command passes, probe-backed paths bypass the new executability gate
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Gaps from #16598 (merged)

### [medium] pi-agent readiness still fails open on a configured-but-missing ACP command (sibling of the fixed elizaos/codex cases)

plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/task-agent-frameworks.ts:657-662 (origin/develop): `case "pi-agent": return Boolean(readConfigEnvKey("ELIZA_PI_AGENT_ACP_COMMAND")) || hasBinaryOnPath("pi-agent")` — the exact pre-PR pattern the same commit replaced for elizaos (649-656) and codex (664-669) with isCommandExecutableAvailable(). pi-agent is a first-class STANDARD_FRAMEWORKS entry (task-agent-frameworks.ts:213-219); installed feeds authReady directly for native adapters (780-782) and the preferred-framework scoring, and the spawn path honors the same key via the generic override in acp-service.ts:3103-3108, so a broken ELIZA_PI_AGENT_ACP_COMMAND advertises a ready framework whose spawn ENOENTs. The PR's new tests (task-agent-frameworks.test.ts:220-281) cover codex + elizaos only.

**Fix direction:** Mirror the fixed cases: `const configured = readConfigEnvKey("ELIZA_PI_AGENT_ACP_COMMAND"); return configured ? isCommandExecutableAvailable(configured) : hasBinaryOnPath("pi-agent");` plus a fail-closed test twinning the codex one.

### [medium] New fail-closed check is dead on all probe-backed discovery paths: AcpService preflight hardcodes installed:true and overrides hasFrameworkBinary

plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/acp-service.ts:2449-2456 (origin/develop): getAvailableAgents() returns `installed: true` unconditionally for DEFAULT_AGENTS = ["elizaos", "codex", "claude", "opencode"] (line 735), and checkAvailableAgents (2458-2463) just filters it. task-agent-frameworks.ts:770-773 computes `installed = preflight?.installed === true || hasFrameworkBinary(id) || nativeExplicit` — the preflight short-circuit wins, so the PR's executability check never runs when a probe is passed. Production passes AcpService as the probe in three places: providers/active-workspace-context.ts:63, providers/action-examples.ts:45-48, and api/agent-routes.ts:469-472 (GET /api/coding-agents/settings). Only the static no-probe path (providers/available-agents.ts:85) is protected, so the planner context and the settings API still report a missing configured Codex/Eliza ACP executable as installed — the exact condition the PR set out to fail closed — and the two discovery caches 

**Fix direction:** Make AcpService.getAvailableAgents report real installability (reuse hasFrameworkBinary / isCommandExecutableAvailable per adapter) or stop treating a probe's installed:true as authoritative over a failed local executability check (e.g. `preflight?.installed === true && hasFrameworkBinary(id)` for adapters with a configured command).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] pi-agent readiness fails closed on a configured-but-missing ACP command (mirror of the fixed elizaos-code check)
- [ ] The executability gate is enforced on probe-backed discovery paths (AcpService preflight no longer hardcodes installed=true)
- [ ] (low) `ELIZA_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE` explicit selection goes through the same gate

topPRs.title: fix(ci): align Biome 2.5.4 and make lint gates read-only
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- align the effective repository Biome toolchain on 2.5.4 across the root override, lockfile, schemas, workspace manifests, standalone plugin locks, and generated-project templates
- add a fail-closed version-consistency guard and template contracts so package/scaffold drift cannot silently return
- restore the deterministic Biome 2.5.4 format and lint closure across the repository; the large mechanical portion is the canonical formatter output introduced by 2.5.4
- make required CI lint lanes read-only (`lint:check`) so lint can no longer mutate files before `format:check` and create a false-green gate
- harden the merge-gate contract against conditional, dependency, empty-matrix, failure-masking, alternate-YAML-key, comment-boundary, shell, and working-directory bypasses
- isolate every changed Bun coverage suite in its own process, then union-merge its LCOV line hits so process-global module mocks cannot create order-dependent failures without losing complementary coverage
- repair the script-audit and scaffold contract gaps exposed while running the complete root verification

Fixes #16730.

Biome 2.5.4 behavior reference: https://biomejs.dev/internals/changelog/version/2-5-4/

## Exact-head validation

Base: `f1ae987164bdf9ec0fcba13f5a446daed99b39e4`  
Head: `b3f01a16a95f83574bef751a7f3f470a81b390e5`  
Diff: 286 files, 4,988 insertions, 2,998 deletions

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: passed; 5,056 installs checked with no dependency changes
- `bun.lock` SHA-256 before/after install: `5cc00f8613d58d87e37c7fbb676da38526995e2c0bc3f064761fb3f838f48f01`
- `bun run verify`: passed on the exact tree
  - agent/CLAUDE parity: 297 tracked pairs passed
  - type-safety, error-policy, voice-policy, view-action, and alias-read ratchets passed
  - Turbo typecheck + read-only lint: 573/573 tasks passed across 252 packages
  - build-model, Turbo dependency, secret-leak, script, and test-realness audits passed
  - dist-path consumers: 28/28 configurations passed
- `bun run lint:check`: 233/233 read-only tasks passed
- `bun run format:check`: 240/240 read-only tasks passed
- changed-file coverage reproduction:
  - classifier selected 1 registered Node self-test, 35 Bun tests, and 135 Vitest tests on the final tree
  - all 35 Bun files passed in independent Bun 1.3.14 processes with `--conditions=eliza-source` and LCOV enabled
  - 35 isolated LCOV reports union-merged into one logical Bun report; merger sources cleared the enforced floor at 65.79% and 63.64%
  - complementary-coverage regression proves 30% + 30% line hits become 60%, removes isolated inputs, and preserves the best-lane comparison between merged Bun and Vitest reports
- focused coverage/version/scaffold contracts: passed; coverage workflow 4/4, LCOV/Vitest grouping 8/8, combined focused suite 27/27
- coverage-gate and changed-file-classifier self-tests: passed
- Biome version-consistency guard: passed
- merge-gate contract: 52/52 adversarial self-test cases passed; live workflow contract passed
- `actionlint` passed on all changed workflows, including both protected gates and the coverage workflow
- independent adversarial reviews: no actionable findings; duplicate-key and unsupported YAML merge-key overrides were confirmed invalid, and the final process-isolation/LCOV-union implementation was reviewed independently
- `git diff --check`: passed; verification-generated shadows/declarations and local coverage output removed; worktree clean

## Scope and review notes

The product-facing source changes are limited to type-safe fixes required by the 2.5.4 lint closure. The remainder is deterministic formatting, toolchain/version synchronization, scaffold consistency, CI contract hardening, and a fail-closed repair for Bun's process-global module mocks in the changed-file coverage lane. No test is skipped, removed, or weakened. This PR will not merge until the fresh exact-head GitHub checks complete successfully.

topPRs.title: fix(app): unblock composed iOS auth and full-Bun smoke
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- run the scheduled iOS Local lane through the canonical composition: fresh simulator app install, OS-delivered auth callback, then the strict full-Bun local-model probe
- write/read Capacitor preferences inside the simulator domain, repair the Xcode 16.4 simulator Swift-library lookup for `simctl` children, and pre-approve the app's URL scheme without replacing unrelated LaunchServices entries
- share one strict app-core full-Bun probe with the renderer, preserve the exact model input/output receipt, and render an explicit terminal pass/fail state only after the terminal receipt is persisted
- split platform entrypoint seams into source modules with honest source-path tests; changed-source coverage passes without a classifier or policy exemption
- hard-gate the redacted scheme/auth/model receipts, exact head and model hashes, unified logs, JPG, and H.264 MP4

Addresses #13577. Scoped contribution to #13562.

## Root cause and repair

The hosted lane exposed three independent simulator boundaries in sequence:

1. A host-path `defaults write` could exit successfully without producing simulator-readable Capacitor Preferences. The lane now executes `xcrun simctl spawn <udid> defaults ...`, supports Capacitor's prefixed key plus its raw alias, and requires a native readback before launch.
2. Xcode 16.4 with the iOS 18.5 simulator could launch-abort while resolving `/usr/lib/swift/libswiftWebKit.dylib`. The workflow supplies Apple's simulator-runtime Cryptex fallback only to `simctl` child processes; it does not change the production deployment target.
3. A fresh simulator presented an untappable `Open in “Eliza”?` sheet for `simctl openurl`, leaving auth at `phase=requested`. The orchestrator now preserves the existing LaunchServices dictionary, writes and reads back `com.apple.CoreSimulator.CoreSimulatorBridge-->elizaos = ai.elizaos.app`, emits a redacted receipt, and reboots once when that mapping changes.

Mutation-sensitive contracts prove unapproved=`confirmation-blocked`, approved=`deliver-to-app`, wrong-bundle repair, idempotence, simulator-native preference readback, and the complete strict non-streaming + streaming model contract.

## Exact-head hosted result

Commit `8359d9a093b46574127f40a5e10819399ce8fc8e` ran in [Mobile Build Smoke 29316042667](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29316042667). The target [iOS Local (full-Bun) Simulator Smoke job 87030207735](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29316042667/job/87030207735) passed every step, including the composed auth + full-Bun E2E.

- artifact `ios-auth-full-bun-e2e`, ID `8304361098`, ZIP SHA-256 `28541bb5aac540136b1a97a6c4c23a9a62e054c1a34d64bb86e686fe8fef5544`
- fresh install receipt passed; renderer build stamp was checked before and after install
- scheme receipt: `changed=true`, `callbackDisposition=deliver-to-app`, `rebooted=true`, with no filesystem path leaked
- auth classification: `synthetic_callback_rejected`, `accepted=false`, `sessionEstablished=false`, and no server before/after — this lane proves OS delivery and handler classification, not login
- runtime: `Bun`, bridge `bun-ios:3`, transport `bun-host-ipc`; active `eliza-1-2b` status `ready` through `capacitor-llama`
- exact model input: `In one short sentence, confirm the iOS full Bun local backend is running.` (`DM`, source `ios-local`)
- exact non-stream and stream output: `The iOS full Bun local backend is running.`; model latency `4417 ms`
- terminal pixel state: `iOS full Bun backend smoke passed.`

The overall workflow is red because its separate regular iOS onboarding → remote-Mac mixed-content job timed out with WebSocket state `disconnected`. That job built and launched a different cloud-mode app path. The target full-Bun job above is successful and its required artifacts are complete.

## Validation

- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/app test` — 543 Bun script tests + 571 Vitest tests passed
- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/app-core test` — 1,216 passed, 8 skipped
- [x] focused hosted-contract/mobile-smoke tests — 39/39 passed
- [x] app + app-core typechecks and app production build
- [x] `bun run verify` — 573/573 Turbo tasks plus dependency/build/test-realness checks and 28 dist-consumer typechecks
- [x] [exact-head changed-source coverage](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29316030405) — 8/8 production sources, 84.31% mean, 50.57% minimum (`main.tsx`), 83.94% iOS runtime bridge, no exemption

topPRs.title: docs(fleet): propose federated agent charter
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Proposes one implementation-ready coordination contract for Sol, Nubs' agent, Shaw's agent, and future team agents.

This is additive and does not replace or edit `.github/FLEET.md`. It includes:

- canonical work, team, agent, and session identity
- TTL leases with renewal, fencing generations, and zombie reclamation
- pillar ownership plus exactly one accountable owner per failure class
- typed dependency and collision graph with deterministic dispatch
- two-phase handoffs and immutable evidence/review receipts
- independent review, merge authority, and HITL rules
- strict Smithers vs Merge Steward authority boundary
- GitHub-now and Forgejo-later adapters with a single write-authority epoch
- JSON Schema and network-free deterministic conformance tests

## Why

The proposal is grounded in observed collisions: the parallel FLEET/AGENT_COORDINATION governance split, concurrent Seeker builds, stale prod-deploy takeover, branch rescue overlap, lane-tag identity confusion, board/discussion/PR drift, and potential Smithers/Merge Steward split-brain.

## Test evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --test scripts/federated-agent-charter-conformance.test.mjs` | Draft 2020-12 schema validation + requirements 1-20 + 14 GAP negative tests, all passing |
| `python3 -m json.tool docs/federated-agent-charter.schema.json` | passed |
| `git diff --check` | passed |
| third-party services | none used by tests |

## Evidence

<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- Before screenshots: N/A - documentation/schema/test-only governance proposal; no UI surface exists or is changed by this PR (only `docs/*.md`, `docs/*.schema.json`, and a `scripts/*.test.mjs` conformance suite).
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- After screenshots: N/A - no UI surface changed; this PR adds a charter document, its JSON Schema, and a network-free conformance test only.
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- Walkthrough video: N/A - no user-facing flow; the deliverable is a governance contract plus its executable schema/conformance check.
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->
- Backend logs: N/A - no runtime service or backend code path is added or modified; nothing executes at runtime.
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- Frontend console/network logs: N/A - no frontend code changed; there is no request/response or client state change to capture.
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- Real-LLM trajectory: N/A - no agent prompt, model, provider, evaluator, or action behavior is changed; this is a static governance/schema/test artifact.
<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->
- Domain artifacts: the governance artifacts themselves are the deliverable and are checked into this PR: [charter](docs/FEDERATED-AGENT-CHARTER-2026-07-20.md), [JSON Schema](docs/federated-agent-charter.schema.json), and [conformance suite](scripts/federated-agent-charter-conformance.test.mjs). The conformance suite validates the canonical fixture against the Draft 2020-12 schema and executes all 20 requirements plus 14 `GAP:` negative regressions via `node --test scripts/federated-agent-charter-conformance.test.mjs`.

## Review and merge policy

Governance/workflow proposal. **Manual merge only.** This PR must not self-merge or auto-merge. Maintainers should decide whether and how it becomes canonical relative to `.github/FLEET.md` and the unresolved Eliza Hub ownership boundary in #16436.

No existing Nubs or Shaw files are modified.

[sol-orch]
